lines.lat: In nómine Patris, et Fílii, et Spíritus Sancti.
lines.eng: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

lines.lat: Amen.
lines.eng: Amen.

lines.lat: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum.
lines.eng: Our Father, Who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name.

lines.lat: Advéniat regnum tuum. Fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra.
lines.eng: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

lines.lat: Panem nostrum quotidiánum da nobis hódie,
lines.eng: Give us this day our daily bread,

lines.lat: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris.
lines.eng: and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

lines.lat: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo.
lines.eng: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.

lines.lat: ℟. Amen.
lines.eng: ℟. Amen.

lines.lat: Ave María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum.
lines.eng: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.

lines.lat: Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui, Iesus.
lines.eng: Blessed art thou amongst women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

lines.lat: ℟. Sancta María, Mater Dei, ora pro nobis peccatóribus,
lines.eng: ℟. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners,

lines.lat: nunc et in hora mortis nostræ. Amen.
lines.eng: now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

lines.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
lines.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

lines.lat: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper,
lines.eng: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be,

lines.lat: et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.eng: world without end. Amen.

title: Oratio Fátimæ
note: Added after each Gloria Patri in the Rosary, as revealed by Our Lady at Fatima in 1917.

lines.lat: O mi Iesu, dimítte nobis débita nostra,
lines.eng: O my Jesus, forgive us our sins,

lines.lat: líbera nos ab igne inférni,
lines.eng: save us from the fires of hell,

lines.lat: perduc in cælum omnes ánimas,
lines.eng: lead all souls to Heaven,

lines.lat: præsértim eas, quæ misericórdiæ tuæ máxime índigent. Amen.
lines.eng: especially those most in need of Thy mercy. Amen.

title: Salve Regína
note: Said at the end of the Rosary, and as the Marian antiphon of Compline from Trinity Sunday through Advent.

lines.lat: Salve, Regína, Mater misericórdiæ,
lines.eng: Hail, holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

lines.lat: vita, dulcédo et spes nostra, salve.
lines.eng: our life, our sweetness, and our hope, hail.

lines.lat: Ad te clamámus, éxsules fílii Hevæ.
lines.eng: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

lines.lat: Ad te suspirámus, geméntes et flentes in hac lacrimárum valle.
lines.eng: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears.

lines.lat: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra, illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
lines.eng: Turn then, most gracious Advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us.

lines.lat: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui, nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
lines.eng: And after this our exile, show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

lines.lat: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María. Amen.
lines.eng: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary. Amen.

title: Credo Apostolórum
note: Said at the beginning of the Rosary, holding the crucifix.

lines.lat: Credo in Deum Patrem omnipoténtem, Creatórem cæli et terræ.
lines.eng: I believe in God, the Father Almighty, Creator of heaven and earth.

lines.lat: Et in Iesum Christum, Fílium eius únicum, Dóminum nostrum:
lines.eng: And in Jesus Christ, His only Son, our Lord:

lines.lat: qui concéptus est de Spíritu Sancto, natus ex María Vírgine,
lines.eng: Who was conceived by the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary,

lines.lat: passus sub Póntio Piláto, crucifíxus, mórtuus, et sepúltus:
lines.eng: suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died, and was buried.

lines.lat: descéndit ad ínferos; tértia die resurréxit a mórtuis;
lines.eng: He descended into hell; the third day He rose again from the dead;

lines.lat: ascéndit ad cælos; sedet ad déxteram Dei Patris omnipoténtis:
lines.eng: He ascended into heaven, and sitteth at the right hand of God the Father Almighty:

lines.lat: inde ventúrus est iudicáre vivos et mórtuos.
lines.eng: from thence He shall come to judge the living and the dead.

lines.lat: Credo in Spíritum Sanctum, sanctam Ecclésiam cathólicam,
lines.eng: I believe in the Holy Ghost, the Holy Catholic Church,

lines.lat: Sanctórum communiónem, remissiónem peccatórum,
lines.eng: the communion of Saints, the forgiveness of sins,

lines.lat: carnis resurrectiónem, vitam ætérnam. Amen.
lines.eng: the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting. Amen.

title: Confíteor
note: Said at the foot of the altar at the beginning of Mass, and at Compline.

lines.lat: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini,
lines.eng: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin,

lines.lat: beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ,
lines.eng: to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist,

lines.lat: sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis,
lines.eng: to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints,

lines.lat: quia peccávi nimis cogitatióne, verbo et ópere:
lines.eng: that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word, and deed:

lines.lat: mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa.
lines.eng: through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault.

lines.lat: Ideo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum,
lines.eng: Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel,

lines.lat: beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos,
lines.eng: blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints,

lines.lat: oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum. Amen.
lines.eng: to pray for me to the Lord our God. Amen.

title: Kýrie Eléison
note: Said in three groups of three at the beginning of Mass.

lines.lat: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.eng: Lord, have mercy.

lines.lat: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.eng: Lord, have mercy.

lines.lat: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.eng: Lord, have mercy.

lines.lat: Christe, eléison.
lines.eng: Christ, have mercy.

lines.lat: Christe, eléison.
lines.eng: Christ, have mercy.

lines.lat: Christe, eléison.
lines.eng: Christ, have mercy.

lines.lat: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.eng: Lord, have mercy.

lines.lat: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.eng: Lord, have mercy.

lines.lat: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.eng: Lord, have mercy.

title: Glória in Excélsis Deo
eng: Glory to God in the Highest
note: The Greater Doxology. Sung at Mass on Sundays (outside Advent and Lent), feasts, and within octaves.

lines.lat: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis.
lines.eng: Glory be to God on high, and on earth peace to men of good will.

lines.lat: Laudámus te. Benedícimus te. Adorámus te. Glorificámus te.
lines.eng: We praise Thee. We bless Thee. We adore Thee. We glorify Thee.

lines.lat: Grátias ágimus tibi propter magnam glóriam tuam.
lines.eng: We give Thee thanks for Thy great glory.

lines.lat: Dómine Deus, Rex cæléstis, Deus Pater omnípotens.
lines.eng: O Lord God, heavenly King, God the Father almighty.

lines.lat: Dómine Fili Unigénite, Iesu Christe. Dómine Deus, Agnus Dei, Fílius Patris.
lines.eng: O Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son. O Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father.

lines.lat: Qui tollis peccáta mundi, miserére nobis.
lines.eng: Thou Who takest away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.

lines.lat: Qui tollis peccáta mundi, súscipe deprecatiónem nostram.
lines.eng: Thou Who takest away the sins of the world, receive our prayer.

lines.lat: Qui sedes ad déxteram Patris, miserére nobis.
lines.eng: Thou Who sittest at the right hand of the Father, have mercy on us.

lines.lat: Quóniam tu solus Sanctus. Tu solus Dóminus. Tu solus Altíssimus, Iesu Christe.
lines.eng: For Thou alone art holy. Thou alone art the Lord. Thou alone art the most high, Jesus Christ.

lines.lat: Cum Sancto Spíritu, in glória Dei Patris. Amen.
lines.eng: With the Holy Ghost, in the glory of God the Father. Amen.

title: Sanctus
note: Sung at every Mass before the Canon. All kneel.

lines.lat: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus, Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
lines.eng: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Hosts.

lines.lat: Pleni sunt cæli et terra glória tua.
lines.eng: Heaven and earth are full of Thy glory.

lines.lat: Hosánna in excélsis.
lines.eng: Hosanna in the highest.

lines.lat: ✠ Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini.
lines.eng: ✠ Blessed is He Who cometh in the name of the Lord.

lines.lat: Hosánna in excélsis.
lines.eng: Hosanna in the highest.

title: Agnus Dei
note: Said before Communion.

lines.lat: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccáta mundi: miserére nobis.
lines.eng: Lamb of God, Who takest away the sins of the world: have mercy on us.

lines.lat: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccáta mundi: miserére nobis.
lines.eng: Lamb of God, Who takest away the sins of the world: have mercy on us.

lines.lat: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccáta mundi: dona nobis pacem.
lines.eng: Lamb of God, Who takest away the sins of the world: grant us peace.

title: Dómine, Non Sum Dignus
note: Said three times before receiving Holy Communion, striking the breast at each repetition.

lines.lat: Dómine, non sum dignus, ut intres sub tectum meum:
lines.eng: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof:

lines.lat: sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur ánima mea.
lines.eng: but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed.

lines.lat: (Said three times.)
lines.eng: (Said three times.)

title: Oblátio Matutína
note: Traditionally said upon rising, to consecrate the day's prayers, works, joys, and sufferings to the Sacred Heart of Jesus through the Immaculate Heart of Mary.

lines.lat: O Iesu, per Cor Immaculátum Maríæ,
lines.eng: O Jesus, through the Immaculate Heart of Mary,

lines.lat: óffero tibi oratiónes, ópera, gáudia et labóres huius diéi
lines.eng: I offer Thee the prayers, works, joys, and sufferings of this day

lines.lat: in satisfactiónem pro peccátis nostris,
lines.eng: in satisfaction for our sins,

lines.lat: in ómnibus Missis Sacrificiis hódie per orbem celebrátis,
lines.eng: in union with all the Holy Sacrifices of the Mass celebrated throughout the world today,

lines.lat: pro ómnibus intentiónibus Sacratíssimi Cordis tui,
lines.eng: for all the intentions of Thy Most Sacred Heart,

lines.lat: pro unióne christianórum, pro conversióne peccatórum,
lines.eng: for the reunion of all Christians, for the conversion of sinners,

lines.lat: ac pro intentiónibus Summi Pontíficis hoc mense. Amen.
lines.eng: and for the intentions of our Holy Father this month. Amen.

title: Memoráre
note: A prayer to Our Lady by St. Bernard of Clairvaux (12th century).

lines.lat: Memoráre, O piíssima Virgo María, non esse audítum a sǽculo,
lines.eng: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known

lines.lat: quemquam ad tua curréntem præsídia, tua implorántem auxília, tua peténtem suffrágia,
lines.eng: that anyone who fled to thy protection, implored thy help, or sought thine intercession,

lines.lat: esse derelíctum.
lines.eng: was left unaided.

lines.lat: Ego tali animátus confidéntia, ad te, Virgo Vírginum, Mater, curro,
lines.eng: Inspired by this confidence, I fly unto thee, O Virgin of virgins, my Mother;

lines.lat: ad te vénio, coram te gemens peccátor assísto.
lines.eng: to thee do I come, before thee I stand, sinful and sorrowful.

lines.lat: Noli, Mater Verbi, verba mea despícere,
lines.eng: O Mother of the Word Incarnate, despise not my petitions,

lines.lat: sed áudi propítia et exáudi. Amen.
lines.eng: but in thy mercy hear and answer me. Amen.

title: Actus Contritiónis
note: The traditional Latin Act of Contrition, distinct from the English form ('O my God, I am heartily sorry…') but equally valid. Said daily and in the Sacrament of Penance.

lines.lat: Deus meus, ex toto corde pǽnitet me ómnium meórum peccatórum,
lines.eng: My God, with my whole heart I repent of all my sins,

lines.lat: éaque detéstor, quia peccándo,
lines.eng: and I detest them, because by sinning

lines.lat: non solum pœnas a te iuste statútas proméritus sum,
lines.eng: I have not only deserved the punishments justly decreed by Thee,

lines.lat: sed præsértim quia offéndi te, summum bonum, ac dignum qui super ómnia diligáris.
lines.eng: but above all because I have offended Thee, the supreme good, worthy to be loved above all things.

lines.lat: Ideo fírmiter propóno, adiuvánte grátia tua,
lines.eng: Therefore I firmly resolve, with the help of Thy grace,

lines.lat: de cétero me non peccatúrum peccandíque occasiónes próximas fugitúrum. Amen.
lines.eng: henceforth to sin no more and to flee the near occasions of sin. Amen.

title: Ánima Christi
note: A prayer of thanksgiving after Holy Communion, often attributed to St. Ignatius of Loyola.

lines.lat: Ánima Christi, sanctífica me.
lines.eng: Soul of Christ, sanctify me.

lines.lat: Corpus Christi, salva me.
lines.eng: Body of Christ, save me.

lines.lat: Sanguis Christi, inébria me.
lines.eng: Blood of Christ, inebriate me.

lines.lat: Aqua láteris Christi, lava me.
lines.eng: Water from the side of Christ, wash me.

lines.lat: Pássio Christi, confórta me.
lines.eng: Passion of Christ, strengthen me.

lines.lat: O bone Iesu, exáudi me.
lines.eng: O good Jesus, hear me.

lines.lat: Intra tua vúlnera abscónde me.
lines.eng: Within Thy wounds hide me.

lines.lat: Ne permíttas me separári a te.
lines.eng: Permit me not to be separated from Thee.

lines.lat: Ab hoste malígno defénde me.
lines.eng: From the malignant enemy defend me.

lines.lat: In hora mortis meæ voca me.
lines.eng: In the hour of my death call me.

lines.lat: Et iube me veníre ad te,
lines.eng: And bid me come unto Thee,

lines.lat: ut cum Sanctis tuis laudem te,
lines.eng: that with Thy saints I may praise Thee,

lines.lat: ℟. in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.eng: ℟. for ever and ever. Amen.

title: En Ego, O Bone Iesu
note: To be said after Communion, kneeling before a crucifix. A plenary indulgence may be gained on any Friday in Lent.

lines.lat: En ego, o bone et dulcíssime Iesu, ante conspéctum tuum génibus me provólvo,
lines.eng: Behold, O good and most sweet Jesus, I cast myself upon my knees in Thy sight,

lines.lat: ac máximo ánimi ardóre te oro atque obtéstor,
lines.eng: and with the most fervent desire of my soul I pray and beseech Thee

lines.lat: ut meum in cor vívidos fídei, spei et caritátis sensus,
lines.eng: that Thou wouldst impress upon my heart lively sentiments of faith, hope, and charity,

lines.lat: atque veram peccatórum meórum pæniténtiam,
lines.eng: with true contrition for my sins,

lines.lat: éaque emendándi firmíssimam voluntátem velis imprímere;
lines.eng: and a firm purpose of amendment;

lines.lat: dum magno ánimi afféctu et dolóre tua quinque vúlnera mecum ipse consídero,
lines.eng: while with deep affection and grief of soul I ponder within myself and mentally contemplate Thy five most precious wounds,

lines.lat: illud præ óculis habens, quod iam in ore ponébat tuo David Prophéta de te, o bone Iesu:
lines.eng: having before my eyes that which Thy prophet David spake concerning Thee, O good Jesus:

lines.lat: Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos: dinumeravérunt ómnia ossa mea. (Ps 21:17-18)
lines.eng: They have pierced my hands and my feet; they have numbered all my bones. (Ps 21:17-18)

lines.lat: ℟. Amen.
lines.eng: ℟. Amen.

title: Tantum Ergo Sacraméntum
note: The last two stanzas of the Pange Lingua by St. Thomas Aquinas. Sung at Benediction of the Blessed Sacrament.

lines.lat: Tantum ergo Sacraméntum venerémur cérnui:
lines.eng: Therefore we, before Him bending, this great Sacrament revere:

lines.lat: et antíquum documéntum novo cedat rítui:
lines.eng: types and shadows have their ending, for the newer rite is here.

lines.lat: præstet fides suppleméntum sénsuum deféctui.
lines.eng: Faith, our outward sense befriending, makes our inward vision clear.

lines.lat: Genitóri, Genitóque laus et iubilátio,
lines.eng: Glory let us give, and blessing, to the Father and the Son;

lines.lat: salus, honor, virtus quoque sit et benedíctio:
lines.eng: honour, might, and praise addressing, while eternal ages run;

lines.lat: procedénti ab utróque compar sit laudátio. Amen.
lines.eng: ever too His love confessing, Who from both with both is One. Amen.

lines.lat: ℣. Panem de cælo præstitísti eis.
lines.eng: ℣. Thou hast given them bread from Heaven.

lines.lat: ℟. Omne delectaméntum in se habéntem.
lines.eng: ℟. Containing in itself all sweetness.

title: Oratio ad Sanctum Michaélem
eng: Prayer to St. Michael the Archangel
note: Composed by Pope Leo XIII in 1886 after a vision of the spiritual warfare facing the Church. Said after Low Mass until 1965, and widely revived today.

lines.lat: Sancte Míchaël Archángele, defénde nos in prǽlio;
lines.eng: St. Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle;

lines.lat: contra nequítiam et insídias diáboli esto præsídium.
lines.eng: be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil.

lines.lat: Ímperet illi Deus, súpplices deprecámur:
lines.eng: May God rebuke him, we humbly pray:

lines.lat: tuque, Princeps milítiæ cæléstis,
lines.eng: and do thou, O Prince of the heavenly host,

lines.lat: Sátanam aliósque spíritus malígnos,
lines.eng: by the power of God cast into hell Satan

lines.lat: qui ad perditiónem animárum pervagántur in mundo,
lines.eng: and all the evil spirits who prowl about the world

lines.lat: divína virtúte, in inférnum detrúde. Amen.
lines.eng: seeking the ruin of souls. Amen.

title: Adóro Te Devóte
note: A Eucharistic hymn by St. Thomas Aquinas, said in thanksgiving after Communion.

lines.lat: Adóro te devóte, latens Déitas,
lines.eng: I devoutly adore Thee, O hidden God,

lines.lat: quæ sub his figúris vere látitas:
lines.eng: truly hidden beneath these appearances:

lines.lat: tibi se cor meum totum súbiicit,
lines.eng: my whole heart submits to Thee,

lines.lat: quia te contémplans totum déficit.
lines.eng: and in contemplating Thee, it surrenders itself completely.

lines.lat: Visus, tactus, gustus in te fállitur,
lines.eng: Sight, touch, taste are all deceived in their judgment of Thee,

lines.lat: sed audítu solo tuto créditur:
lines.eng: but hearing suffices firmly to believe:

lines.lat: credo quidquid dixit Dei Fílius;
lines.eng: I believe all that the Son of God has spoken;

lines.lat: nil hoc verbo veritátis vérius.
lines.eng: there is nothing truer than this Word of Truth.

lines.lat: In cruce latébat sola Déitas,
lines.eng: On the cross only the Divinity was hidden,

lines.lat: at hic latet simul et humánitas:
lines.eng: but here the Humanity is also concealed:

lines.lat: ambo tamen credens atque cónfitens,
lines.eng: yet believing and confessing both,

lines.lat: peto quod petívit latro pǽnitens.
lines.eng: I ask for what the penitent thief asked.

lines.lat: Plagas, sicut Thomas, non intúeor:
lines.eng: I do not see the wounds, as Thomas did,

lines.lat: Deum tamen meum te confíteor.
lines.eng: yet I confess Thee to be my God.

lines.lat: Fac me tibi semper magis crédere,
lines.eng: Make me believe Thee ever more and more,

lines.lat: in te spem habére, te dilígere.
lines.eng: place all my hope in Thee, and love Thee with all my heart.

lines.lat: O memoriále mortis Dómini!
lines.eng: O memorial of our Lord's death!

lines.lat: Panis vivus, vitam præstans hómini!
lines.eng: Living Bread, that givest life to man!

lines.lat: Præsta meæ menti de te vívere,
lines.eng: Grant my soul henceforth on Thee to live,

lines.lat: et te illi semper dulce sápere.
lines.eng: and ever a sweet savour of Thee to have.

lines.lat: Pie pellicáne, Iesu Dómine,
lines.eng: O loving Pelican, O Jesus Lord,

lines.lat: me immúndum munda tuo sánguine:
lines.eng: unclean I am, but cleanse me in Thy blood:

lines.lat: cuius una stilla salvum fácere
lines.eng: of which a single drop, for sinners spilt,

lines.lat: totum mundum quit ab ómni scélere.
lines.eng: can purge the entire world from all its guilt.

lines.lat: Iesu, quem velátum nunc aspício,
lines.eng: O Jesus, Whom for the present veiled I see,

lines.lat: oro, fiat illud quod tam sítio:
lines.eng: what I so thirst for, oh, vouchsafe to me:

lines.lat: ut te reveláta cernens fácie,
lines.eng: that I may see Thy countenance unfolding,

lines.lat: visu sim beátus tuæ glóriæ. Amen.
lines.eng: and may be blest Thy glory in beholding. Amen.

title: Súscipe
note: The prayer of total self-offering by St. Ignatius of Loyola, from the Spiritual Exercises. One of the most radical acts of surrender in the Catholic tradition.

lines.lat: Súscipe, Dómine, univérsam meam libertátem.
lines.eng: Take, Lord, and receive all my liberty,

lines.lat: Accipe memóriam, intelléctum atque voluntátem omnem.
lines.eng: my memory, my understanding, and my entire will,

lines.lat: Quidquid hábeo vel possídeo, mihi largítus es;
lines.eng: all that I have and possess. Thou hast given it all to me;

lines.lat: id tibi totum restítuo, ac tuæ prorsus voluntáti trado gubernándum.
lines.eng: to Thee, O Lord, I return it. All is Thine; dispose of it wholly according to Thy will.

lines.lat: Amórem tui solum cum grátia tua mihi dones,
lines.eng: Give me only Thy love and Thy grace;

lines.lat: et dives sum satis, nec áliud quidquam ultra posco.
lines.eng: that is enough for me, and I ask for nothing more.

title: Angelus Dómini
note: Prayed thrice daily (6am, noon, 6pm) to honour the Incarnation. During Eastertide, the Regina Caeli is said instead.

lines.lat: ℣. Angelus Dómini nuntiávit Maríæ,
lines.eng: ℣. The Angel of the Lord declared unto Mary,

lines.lat: ℟. Et concépit de Spíritu Sancto.
lines.eng: ℟. And she conceived of the Holy Ghost.

lines.lat: Ave María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum. Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui, Iesus. Sancta María, Mater Dei, ora pro nobis peccatóribus, nunc et in hora mortis nostræ. Amen.
lines.eng: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

lines.lat: ℣. Ecce ancílla Dómini,
lines.eng: ℣. Behold the handmaid of the Lord,

lines.lat: ℟. Fiat mihi secúndum verbum tuum.
lines.eng: ℟. Be it done unto me according to thy word.

lines.lat: Ave María...
lines.eng: Hail Mary...

lines.lat: ℣. Et Verbum caro factum est,
lines.eng: ℣. And the Word was made flesh,

lines.lat: ℟. Et habitávit in nobis.
lines.eng: ℟. And dwelt among us.

lines.lat: Ave María...
lines.eng: Hail Mary...

lines.lat: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix,
lines.eng: ℣. Pray for us, O holy Mother of God,

lines.lat: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
lines.eng: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

lines.lat: Orémus. Grátiam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, méntibus nostris infúnde; ut qui, Angelo nuntiánte, Christi Fílii tui incarnatiónem cognóvimus, per passiónem eius et crucem ad resurrectiónis glóriam perducámur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.eng: Let us pray. Pour forth, we beseech Thee, O Lord, Thy grace into our hearts; that we, to whom the Incarnation of Christ, Thy Son, was made known by the message of an Angel, may by His Passion and Cross be brought to the glory of His Resurrection. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

title: Regína Cæli
note: Replaces the Angelus during Eastertide (from Easter Sunday to Pentecost Saturday). Said standing, in honour of the Resurrection.

lines.lat: Regína cæli, lætáre, allelúja,
lines.eng: Queen of heaven, rejoice, alleluia,

lines.lat: Quia quem meruísti portáre, allelúja,
lines.eng: For He Whom thou didst merit to bear, alleluia,

lines.lat: Resurréxit, sicut dixit, allelúja.
lines.eng: Has risen, as He said, alleluia.

lines.lat: Ora pro nobis Deum, allelúja.
lines.eng: Pray for us to God, alleluia.

lines.lat: ℣. Gaude et lætáre, Virgo María, allelúja,
lines.eng: ℣. Rejoice and be glad, O Virgin Mary, alleluia,

lines.lat: ℟. Quia surréxit Dóminus vere, allelúja.
lines.eng: ℟. For the Lord has truly risen, alleluia.

lines.lat: Orémus. Deus, qui per resurrectiónem Fílii tui Dómini nostri Iesu Christi mundum lætificáre dignátus es: præsta, quǽsumus; ut per eius Genetrícem Vírginem Maríam perpétuæ capiámus gáudia vitæ. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.eng: Let us pray. O God, Who through the Resurrection of Thy Son our Lord Jesus Christ didst vouchsafe to give joy to the world: grant, we beseech Thee, that through His Mother, the Virgin Mary, we may obtain the joys of everlasting life. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

title: Sub Tuum Præsídium
note: The oldest known Marian prayer, dating to at least the 3rd century. Found on a papyrus fragment from Egypt.

lines.lat: Sub tuum præsídium confúgimus, sancta Dei Génetrix;
lines.eng: We fly to thy protection, O holy Mother of God;

lines.lat: nostras deprecatiónes ne despícias in necessitátibus;
lines.eng: despise not our petitions in our necessities;

lines.lat: sed a perículis cunctis líbera nos semper,
lines.eng: but deliver us always from all dangers,

lines.lat: Virgo gloriósa et benedícta. Amen.
lines.eng: O glorious and blessed Virgin. Amen.

title: De Profúndis
note: One of the seven Penitential Psalms. Prayed especially for the faithful departed and during Lent.

lines.lat: De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine:
lines.eng: Out of the depths I have cried to Thee, O Lord:

lines.lat: Dómine, exáudi vocem meam.
lines.eng: Lord, hear my voice.

lines.lat: Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
lines.eng: Let Thy ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication.

lines.lat: Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine, Dómine, quis sustinébit?
lines.eng: If Thou, O Lord, shalt observe iniquities: Lord, who shall endure it?

lines.lat: Quia apud te propitátio est: et propter legem tuam sustínui te, Dómine.
lines.eng: For with Thee there is merciful forgiveness: and by reason of Thy law, I have waited for Thee, O Lord.

lines.lat: Sustínuit ánima mea in verbo eius: sperávit ánima mea in Dómino.
lines.eng: My soul hath relied on His word: my soul hath hoped in the Lord.

lines.lat: A custódia matutína usque ad noctem, speret Israel in Dómino.
lines.eng: From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord.

lines.lat: Quia apud Dóminum misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
lines.eng: Because with the Lord there is mercy: and with Him plentiful redemption.

lines.lat: Et ipse rédimet Israel ex ómnibus iniquitátibus eius.
lines.eng: And He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.

lines.lat: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine. ℟. Et lux perpétua lúceat eis.
lines.eng: ℣. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord. ℟. And let perpetual light shine upon them.

title: Actus Fídei
note: One of the three theological virtue acts. Traditionally prayed daily, especially in morning prayers.

lines.lat: O Deus, firma fide credo te esse unum Deum in tribus Persónis divínis, Patre et Fílio et Spíritu Sancto.
lines.eng: O my God, I firmly believe that Thou art one God in three divine Persons, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

lines.lat: Credo Iesum Christum, Fílium Dei, incarnátum esse et mortuum pro nobis,
lines.eng: I believe that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, became man and died for us,

lines.lat: qui retríbuet unicuíque, secúndum mérita sua, vitam ætérnam vel poenam ætérnam.
lines.eng: and that He will come to judge the living and the dead, rewarding each according to his merits.

lines.lat: Hæc ómnia credo, quia tu, Deus, ea revelásti, qui nec falli nec fállere potes. Amen.
lines.eng: I believe these and all the truths which the Holy Catholic Church teaches, because Thou hast revealed them, Who canst neither deceive nor be deceived. Amen.

title: Actus Spei
note: One of the three theological virtue acts, expressing trust in God's promises.

lines.lat: O Deus, sperans in promissiónibus tuis, confído te datúrum mihi, per mérita Iesu Christi,
lines.eng: O my God, relying on Thy promises, I trust that Thou wilt grant me, through the merits of Jesus Christ,

lines.lat: vitam ætérnam et grátias necessárias ad eam promeréndam,
lines.eng: eternal life and the graces necessary to obtain it,

lines.lat: per bona ópera quæ ego fácere débeo et propóno. Amen.
lines.eng: through the good works which I ought to do and which I resolve to perform. Amen.

title: Actus Caritátis
note: One of the three theological virtue acts, expressing love of God above all things.

lines.lat: O Deus, amo te super ómnia et ex toto corde meo,
lines.eng: O my God, I love Thee above all things, with my whole heart and soul,

lines.lat: quia tu es summe bonus et infiníte amábilis.
lines.eng: because Thou art all good and worthy of all love.

lines.lat: Amo próximum meum sicut meípsum propter amórem tuum.
lines.eng: I love my neighbour as myself for love of Thee.

lines.lat: Ignósco ómnibus qui me offendérunt, et véniam peto ab ómnibus quos offéndí. Amen.
lines.eng: I forgive all who have injured me, and I ask pardon of all whom I have injured. Amen.

title: Angele Dei
note: A traditional prayer asking for the protection and guidance of one's Guardian Angel. Often taught to children as one of the first prayers learned.

lines.lat: Angele Dei, qui custos es mei,
lines.eng: Angel of God, my guardian dear,

lines.lat: me tibi commíssum pietáte supérna,
lines.eng: to whom God's love commits me here,

lines.lat: hodie illúmina, custódi, rege et gubérna.
lines.eng: ever this day be at my side,

lines.lat: Amen.
lines.eng: to light and guard, to rule and guide. Amen.

title: Benedíctio Mensæ
note: The traditional Latin grace said before meals.

lines.lat: Bénedic, Dómine, nos et hæc tua dona, quæ de tua largitáte sumus sumptúri.
lines.eng: Bless us, O Lord, and these Thy gifts, which we are about to receive from Thy bounty.

lines.lat: Per Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.eng: Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

title: Gratiárum Actio Post Cibum
note: The traditional thanksgiving said after meals.

lines.lat: Ágimus tibi grátias, omnípotens Deus, pro univérsis benefíciis tuis, qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
lines.eng: We give Thee thanks, almighty God, for all Thy benefits, Who livest and reignest for ever and ever.

lines.lat: Amen.
lines.eng: Amen.

lines.lat: Fidélium ánimæ, per misericórdiam Dei, requiéscant in pace.
lines.eng: May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

lines.lat: Amen.
lines.eng: Amen.

title: Miserere
note: Selected verses from the great Penitential Psalm (Psalm 50), prayed before confession and throughout Lent. The psalm of King David after his sin.

lines.lat: Miserére mei, Deus, secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
lines.eng: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy.

lines.lat: Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónium tuárum, dele iniquitátem meam.
lines.eng: And according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies, blot out my iniquity.

lines.lat: Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea, et a peccáto meo munda me.
lines.eng: Wash me yet more from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.

lines.lat: Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco, et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
lines.eng: For I know my iniquity, and my sin is always before me.

lines.lat: Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci.
lines.eng: To Thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before Thee.

lines.lat: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus, et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
lines.eng: Create a clean heart in me, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

lines.lat: Ne proícias me a fácie tua, et Spíritum Sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
lines.eng: Cast me not away from Thy face, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.

lines.lat: Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui, et spíritu principáli confírma me.
lines.eng: Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation, and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

title: Réquiem Ætérnam
note: The traditional prayer for the faithful departed, said after the Rosary and at the end of prayers for the dead.

lines.lat: Réquiem ætérnam dona eis, Dómine.
lines.eng: Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord.

lines.lat: Et lux perpétua lúceat eis.
lines.eng: And let perpetual light shine upon them.

lines.lat: Requiéscant in pace.
lines.eng: May they rest in peace.

lines.lat: Amen.
lines.eng: Amen.

title: Pie Fidélium
eng: Prayer for All the Faithful Departed
note: A brief prayer for all the holy souls in Purgatory.

lines.lat: Fidélium ánimæ, per misericórdiam Dei, requiéscant in pace.
lines.eng: May the souls of all the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

lines.lat: Amen.
lines.eng: Amen.

title: Aspiratiónes in Tentatióne
note: Brief ejaculatory prayers traditionally recommended for moments of temptation.

lines.lat: Iesu, María, Ioseph, assístite mihi in última agónia.
lines.eng: Jesus, Mary, Joseph, assist me in my last agony.

lines.lat: Sancte Míchaël Archángele, defénde nos in prǽlio.
lines.eng: St. Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle.

lines.lat: Cor Iesu sacratíssimum, miserére nobis.
lines.eng: Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, have mercy on us.

lines.lat: Refúgium peccatórum, ora pro nobis.
lines.eng: Refuge of sinners, pray for us.

lines.lat: Dómine, ádiuva me.
lines.eng: Lord, help me.

title: Veni Creátor Spíritus
note: Ancient hymn invoking the Holy Ghost, sung at Pentecost, ordinations, and before important decisions.

lines.lat: Veni, Creátor Spíritus, mentes tuórum vísita, imple supérna grátia, quæ tu creásti péctora.
lines.eng: Come, Holy Ghost, Creator blest, and in our hearts take up Thy rest; come with Thy grace and heavenly aid, to fill the hearts which Thou hast made.

lines.lat: Qui díceris Paráclitus, altíssimi donum Dei, fons vivus, ignis, cáritas, et spiritális únctio.
lines.eng: O Comforter, to Thee we cry, Thou heavenly gift of God most high, Thou fount of life, and fire of love, and sweet anointing from above.

lines.lat: Tu septifórmis múnere, dígitus patérnæ déxteræ, tu rite promíssum Patris, sermóne ditans gúttura.
lines.eng: Thou in Thy sevenfold gifts art known, the finger of God's hand we own; the promise of the Father, Thou, Who dost the tongue with power endow.

lines.lat: Hostem repéllas lóngius, pacémque dones prótinus; ductóre sic te prǽvio, vitémus omne nóxium.
lines.eng: Drive far away our ghostly foe, and Thine abiding peace bestow; if Thou be our preventing guide, no evil can our steps betide.

lines.lat: Per te sciámus da Patrem, noscámus atque Fílium; teque utriúsque Spíritum, credámus omni témpore.
lines.eng: Oh, may Thy grace on us bestow the Father and the Son to know, and Thee through endless times confessed, of both the eternal Spirit blest.

lines.lat: Accénde lumen sénsibus, infúnde amórem córdibus, infírma nostri córporis virtúte firmans pérpeti.
lines.eng: Kindle our senses from above, and make our hearts o'erflow with love; with patience firm and virtue high the weakness of our flesh supply.

lines.lat: Deo Patri sit glória, et Fílio, qui a mórtuis surréxit, ac Paráclito, in sæculórum sǽcula. Amen.
lines.eng: Praise be to Thee, Father and Son, and Holy Spirit, with them one; and may the Son on us bestow the gifts that from the Spirit flow. Amen.

title: Bénedic, Ánima Mea, Dómino
eng: Bless the Lord, O My Soul
note: A short thanksgiving from Psalm 102, suitable as a grace or general thanksgiving.

lines.lat: Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino, et ómnia quæ intra me sunt nómini sancto eius.
lines.eng: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and let all that is within me bless His holy name.

lines.lat: Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino, et noli oblivísci omnes retributiónes eius.
lines.eng: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and never forget all He hath done for thee.

lines.lat: Qui replet in bonis desidérium tuum: renovábitur ut áquilæ iuvéntus tua.
lines.eng: Who satisfieth thy desire with good things: thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle's.

lines.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Amen.
lines.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. Amen.

title: Ad te, beáte Joseph
note: Ordered by Pope Leo XIII to be said after the Rosary in October.

lines.lat: Ad te, beáte Joseph, in tribulatióne nostra confúgimus, atque, imploráto Sponsæ tuæ sanctíssimæ auxílio, patrocínium quoque tuum fidénter expóscimus.
lines.eng: To thee, O blessed Joseph, we have recourse in our tribulation, and having implored the help of thy most holy Spouse, we now, with hearts filled with confidence, earnestly beg thee also to take us under thy protection.

lines.lat: Per eam, quǽsumus, quæ te cum immaculáta Vírgine Dei Genitríce conjúnxit, caritátem, perque patérnum, quo Púerum Iesum ampléxus es, amórem, súpplices deprecámur,
lines.eng: Through that charity wherewith thou wast united to the Immaculate Virgin Mother of God, and through that fatherly love with which thou didst embrace the Child Jesus, we humbly beg thee

lines.lat: ut benignus respícias hereditátem, quam Iesus Christus sánguine suo acquisívit, et necessitátibus nostris tua virtúte et ope succúrras.
lines.eng: to look graciously upon the beloved inheritance which Jesus Christ purchased by His blood, and to aid us in our necessities with thy power and strength.

lines.lat: Tuére, o Custos providentíssime divínæ Famíliæ, Iesu Christi sóbolem eléctam; próhibe a nobis, amantíssime Pater, omnem érrórum ac corruptelárum luem;
lines.eng: Defend, O most watchful guardian of the Holy Family, the chosen children of Jesus Christ; keep from us, O most loving father, every contagion of error and corrupting influence;

lines.lat: propítius nobis, sospitátor noster fortíssime, in pugna cum potestáte tenebrárum de cælo adésto;
lines.eng: mercifully assist us from heaven, O most powerful protector, in our struggle with the power of darkness;

lines.lat: et sicut olim Púerum Iesum e summo erípuisti vitæ discrímine, ita nunc Ecclésiam sanctam Dei ab hostílibus insídiis atque ab omni adversitáte defénde:
lines.eng: and as once thou didst rescue the Child Jesus from deadly peril, so now protect God's Holy Church from the snares of the enemy and from all adversity;

lines.lat: nosque síngulos perpétuo tege patrocínio, ut ad tui exémplum et ope tua suffúlti, sancte vívere, pie émori, sempiternamque in cælis beatitúdinem ássequi possímus. Amen.
lines.eng: shield, too, each one of us by thy constant protection, so that, supported by thy example and thy aid, we may be able to live piously, to die in holiness, and to obtain eternal happiness in heaven. Amen.

title: Commúnio Spirituális
note: Attributed to St. Alphonsus Liguori. Prayed when unable to receive Holy Communion sacramentally.

lines.lat: Mi Iesu, credo te in Sanctíssimo Sacraménto præséntem esse. Amo te super ómnia et desídero te in ánimam meam.
lines.eng: My Jesus, I believe that Thou art present in the Most Blessed Sacrament. I love Thee above all things, and I desire to receive Thee into my soul.

lines.lat: Cum te sacramentáliter recípere non possum, veni saltem spirituáliter in cor meum.
lines.eng: Since I cannot now receive Thee sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart.

lines.lat: Quasi jam advéneris, compléctor te et totum me tibi únio; ne permíttas me a te umquam separári. Amen.
lines.eng: I embrace Thee as if Thou wert already there, and unite myself wholly to Thee. Never permit me to be separated from Thee. Amen.

title: Symbolum Athanasianum
note: Also called the Quicúmque vult. In the 1962 Breviary said at Prime on Trinity Sunday only; in the pre-1955 Breviary said at Prime on Sundays outside the Christmas, Easter, and Pentecost octaves. The asterisk (*) marks the half-verse division between the two choirs.

lines.lat: Quicúmque vult salvus esse, * ante ómnia opus est, ut téneat cathólicam fidem:
lines.eng: Whosoever willeth to be saved, * before all things it is necessary that he hold the Catholic faith.

lines.lat: Quam nisi quisque íntegram inviolatámque serváverit, * absque dúbio in ætérnum períbit.
lines.eng: Which faith except every one do keep whole and undefiled, * without doubt he shall perish eternally.

lines.lat: Fides autem cathólica hæc est: * ut unum Deum in Trinitáte, et Trinitátem in unitáte venerémur.
lines.eng: Now the Catholic faith is this, * that we worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity.

lines.lat: Neque confundéntes persónas, * neque substántiam separántes.
lines.eng: Neither confounding the Persons, * nor dividing the substance.

lines.lat: Alia est enim persóna Patris, ália Fílii, * ália Spíritus Sancti:
lines.eng: For there is one Person of the Father, another of the Son, * and another of the Holy Ghost.

lines.lat: Sed Patris, et Fílii, et Spíritus Sancti una est divínitas, * æquális glória, coætérna majéstas.
lines.eng: But the Godhead of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost is one, * the Glory Equal, the Majesty Co-Eternal.

lines.lat: Qualis Pater, talis Fílius, * talis Spíritus Sanctus.
lines.eng: Such as the Father is, such is the Son, * and such is the Holy Ghost.

lines.lat: Increátus Pater, increátus Fílius, * increátus Spíritus Sanctus.
lines.eng: The Father Uncreated, the Son Uncreated, * and the Holy Ghost Uncreated.

lines.lat: Imménsus Pater, imménsus Fílius, * imménsus Spíritus Sanctus.
lines.eng: The Father Infinite, the Son Infinite, * and the Holy Ghost Infinite.

lines.lat: Ætérnus Pater, ætérnus Fílius, * ætérnus Spíritus Sanctus.
lines.eng: The Father Eternal, the Son Eternal, * and the Holy Ghost Eternal.

lines.lat: Et tamen non tres ætérni, * sed unus ætérnus.
lines.eng: And yet they are not three Eternals, * but one Eternal.

lines.lat: Sicut non tres increáti, nec tres imménsi, * sed unus increátus, et unus imménsus.
lines.eng: As also they are not three Uncreated, nor three Infinites, * but One Uncreated, and One Infinite.

lines.lat: Simíliter omnípotens Pater, omnípotens Fílius, * omnípotens Spíritus Sanctus.
lines.eng: So likewise the Father is Almighty, the Son Almighty, * and the Holy Ghost Almighty.

lines.lat: Et tamen non tres omnipoténtes, * sed unus omnípotens.
lines.eng: And yet they are not three Almighties, * but One Almighty.

lines.lat: Ita Deus Pater, Deus Fílius, * Deus Spíritus Sanctus.
lines.eng: So the Father is God, the Son God, * and the Holy Ghost God.

lines.lat: Et tamen non tres Dii, * sed unus est Deus.
lines.eng: And yet they are not three Gods, * but One God.

lines.lat: Ita Dóminus Pater, Dóminus Fílius, * Dóminus Spíritus Sanctus.
lines.eng: So the Father is Lord, the Son Lord, * and the Holy Ghost Lord.

lines.lat: Et tamen non tres Dómini, * sed unus est Dóminus.
lines.eng: And yet they are not three Lords, * but One Lord.

lines.lat: Quia, sicut singillátim unamquámque persónam Deum ac Dóminum confitéri christiána veritáte compéllimur: * ita tres Deos aut Dóminos dícere cathólica religióne prohibémur.
lines.eng: For, like as we are compelled by Christian truth to acknowledge every Person by Himself to be God and Lord, * so are we forbidden by the Catholic Religion to say, there be three Gods or three Lords.

lines.lat: Pater a nullo est factus: * nec creátus, nec génitus.
lines.eng: The Father is made of none, * neither created, nor begotten.

lines.lat: Fílius a Patre solo est: * non factus, nec creátus, sed génitus.
lines.eng: The Son is of the Father alone: * not made, nor created, but begotten.

lines.lat: Spíritus Sanctus a Patre et Fílio: * non factus, nec creátus, nec génitus, sed procédens.
lines.eng: The Holy Ghost is of the Father, and the Son: * not made, nor created, nor begotten, but proceeding.

lines.lat: Unus ergo Pater, non tres Patres: unus Fílius, non tres Fílii: * unus Spíritus Sanctus, non tres Spíritus Sancti.
lines.eng: So there is One Father, not three Fathers; one Son, not three Sons; * one Holy Ghost, not three Holy Ghosts.

lines.lat: Et in hac Trinitáte nihil prius aut postérius, nihil majus aut minus: * sed totæ tres persónæ coætérnæ sibi sunt et coæquáles.
lines.eng: And in this Trinity is nothing afore or after, nothing is greater or less; * but the whole three Persons are Co-Eternal together, and Co-Equal.

lines.lat: Ita ut per ómnia, sicut jam supra dictum est, * et únitas in Trinitáte, et Trínitas in unitáte veneránda sit.
lines.eng: So that in all things, as is aforesaid, * the Unity in Trinity, and the Trinity in Unity is to be worshipped.

lines.lat: Qui vult ergo salvus esse, * ita de Trinitáte séntiat.
lines.eng: He therefore that willeth to be safe, * let him thus think of the Trinity.

lines.lat: Sed necessárium est ad ætérnam salútem, * ut Incarnatiónem quoque Dómini nostri Jesu Christi fidéliter credat.
lines.eng: But it is necessary to eternal salvation, * that he also believe faithfully the Incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

lines.lat: Est ergo fides recta ut credámus et confiteámur, * quia Dóminus noster Jesus Christus, Dei Fílius, Deus et homo est.
lines.eng: The right Faith therefore is, that we believe and confess, * that our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, is God and man.

lines.lat: Deus est ex substántia Patris ante sǽcula génitus: * et homo est ex substántia matris in sǽculo natus.
lines.eng: God, of the Substance of the Father, Begotten before the worlds: * and Man, of the substance of His mother, born in the world.

lines.lat: Perféctus Deus, perféctus homo: * ex ánima rationáli et humána carne subsístens.
lines.eng: Perfect God, Perfect Man, * of a reasoning soul and human flesh subsisting.

lines.lat: Æquális Patri secúndum divinitátem: * minor Patre secúndum humanitátem.
lines.eng: Equal to the Father as touching His Godhead, * inferior to the Father as touching His Manhood.

lines.lat: Qui licet Deus sit et homo, * non duo tamen, sed unus est Christus.
lines.eng: Who, although He be God and Man, * yet He is not two, but One Christ.

lines.lat: Unus autem non conversióne divinitátis in carnem, * sed assumptióne humanitátis in Deum.
lines.eng: One, however, not by conversion of the Godhead into Flesh, * but by taking of the Manhood into God.

lines.lat: Unus omníno, non confusióne substántiæ, * sed unitáte persónæ.
lines.eng: One altogether, not by confusion of Substance, * but by Unity of Person.

lines.lat: Nam sicut ánima rationális et caro unus est homo: * ita Deus et homo unus est Christus.
lines.eng: For as the reasoning soul and flesh is one man, * so God and man is One Christ.

lines.lat: Qui passus est pro salúte nostra: descéndit ad ínferos: * tértia die resurréxit a mórtuis.
lines.eng: Who suffered for our salvation, descended into hell, * rose again the third day from the dead.

lines.lat: Ascéndit ad cælos, sedet ad déxteram Dei Patris omnipoténtis: * inde ventúrus est judicáre vivos et mórtuos.
lines.eng: He ascended into heaven, He sitteth on the right hand of the Father, God Almighty, * from whence He shall come to judge the quick and the dead.

lines.lat: Ad cujus advéntum omnes hómines resúrgere habent cum corpóribus suis; * et redditúri sunt de factis própriis ratiónem.
lines.eng: At whose coming all men shall rise again with their bodies, * and shall give account for their own works.

lines.lat: Et qui bona egérunt, ibunt in vitam ætérnam: * qui vero mala, in ignem ætérnum.
lines.eng: And they that have done good shall go into life eternal, * but they that have done evil into eternal fire.

lines.lat: Hæc est fides cathólica, * quam nisi quisque fidéliter firmitérque credíderit, salvus esse non póterit.
lines.eng: This is the Catholic Faith, * which except a man believe faithfully and firmly, he cannot be safe.
